findings.finding: Finance leases are treated two different ways. The bridge deducts the existing 70,973M of finance-lease liabilities as a debt-like claim, which is correct and not double counted (see the minor finding below). But the base sales_to_capital of 0.75 is computed on cash capex minus D&A only, described as 'before finance-lease additions'. D&A is taken net of finance-lease depreciation, but the lease additions themselves are left out. The 10-K lease note (reading/10k_full.txt around line 7408, 'Right-of-use assets obtained in exchange for lease obligations: Finance leases') gives 11,633M in FY2024, 20,511M in FY2025 and 24,608M in FY2026, and the 10-Q gives 5,192M for Q1 FY2027. Adding the 56.8B of FY2024-FY2026 finance-lease additions to the 153.5B of net capex gives 119.9 / 210.3 = 0.57, not 0.78. FY2026 alone is 50.1 / 106.2 = 0.47, not 0.61. So the base 0.75 understates reinvestment by about a quarter during the growth years. The bear's 0.55, described as 'below the FY2026 low', is actually above the lease-inclusive FY2026 figure of 0.47. The fair value of 546 is only 4% above the price of 523, so the table's 'cheap' reading depends on this lever. Future lease-funded datacenter capacity is also left out of reinvestment, including the 364.6B of leases not yet commenced, while the existing leases are deducted as debt. That pairing favors the value.
findings.where: companies/MSFT/inputs.json forecast.overrides sales_to_capital (bear 0.55 / base 0.75 / bull 0.95; position part analyst); evidence pf_capex_fy2024-2026, pf_d_and_a_fy2024-2026, dc_capex_incl_leases_q1fy27
findings.fix: Register the finance-lease ROU additions from the 10-K lease note (FY2024 11,633M, FY2025 20,511M, FY2026 24,608M; source pf_10k) and from the 10-Q (Q1 FY2027 5,192M; pf_10q_20261028). Recompute sales_to_capital as incremental revenue / (cash capex + finance-lease ROU additions - D&A), which gives a three-year figure of about 0.57 and FY2026 of about 0.47. Reset bear, base and bull around that basis, keeping the bear below the lease-inclusive FY2026 low. Rerun ticker-value. The alternative is to stop treating finance leases as debt and treat their payments as operating costs, but one of the two treatments must be chosen and used throughout.

findings.finding: The bear path drops 45% in year 1 (from 523 to 289), and nearly all of that drop is a re-rating, not lower earnings. Bear EPS for FY2028 is 20.78 against the FY2027 annualized figure of 20.70, so EPS is flat. The economics multiple, computed at an assumed ROIC of 0.14, is 13.5-13.7x. That is far below the company's own forward P/E low of 20.8x over 2022-2026 (company_path.own_history low 20.8, median 35.2). The 0.14 ROIC is a hypothesis marked 'unproven'. Its evidence ids (capex, CFO, lease commitments, the OpenAI share) show the size of the capital at risk, not a return of 14%. Bear EPS stays flat for four years (20.78, 21.04, 21.16, 21.11) even though the growth anchor is 8%, because the mature margin falls to 38%, below the FY2021-FY2026 low of 41.6%. Each of these choices can be defended on its own. Stacked together and shown as year 1, they need to be stated next to the result. No company_path flag marks a multiple below own history.
findings.where: companies/MSFT/inputs.json company_path.scenarios.bear (roic 0.14, justification unproven); casefile company_path.scenarios.bear.economics.values / multiple_path; out/table_he.md bear row year 1
findings.fix: State next to the table that the bear's year-1 drop is a re-rating to about 13.7x forward EPS, below the 5-year own low of 20.8x, at a hypothesized incremental ROIC of 14%, and is not an earnings fall. Either ground the 0.14 in a computed lease-inclusive incremental ROIC from MSFT's own figures (operating income change / (capex + finance-lease additions - D&A)) or label it a stress hypothesis in scenario_events.bear.

findings.finding: The capex basis is mixed. dc_capex_incl_leases_q1fy27 is 45.2B ('capital expenditures' as defined on the call). It is cited as evidence for sales_to_capital and sits on the same basis as the >50B Q2 guide (dc_g_capex_q2fy27). The 10-Q gives cash PP&E additions of 39,367M plus finance-lease ROU additions of 5,192M, which totals 44.6B. The 7.4B 'finance leases' figure from the call does not reconcile (39.4 + 7.4 = 46.8B). The historical sales_to_capital uses cash capex only, so a guided capex figure on a lease-inclusive basis is being compared with a cash-only history. This repeats review_trace's major finding, and it affects a driver.
findings.where: gather/documents.json dc_capex_incl_leases_q1fy27, dc_capex_incl_leases_q4fy26, dc_g_capex_q1fy27, dc_g_capex_q2fy27; inputs.json sales_to_capital evidence_ids
findings.fix: Use the 10-Q / 10-K figures as the basis: cash PP&E additions and finance-lease ROU additions as two separate facts. Relabel the 45.2B as 'capex as defined on the call, reconciliation unverified'. Compare the >50B guide only with the lease-inclusive history.

findings.finding: There is no guidance track record, even though both sides are on file. For Q1 FY2027, actual revenue of 92,279M is about 1.021x the guided midpoint of 90.40B, COGS is about 1.00x, opex is below guide, and capex came in at 45.2B against the >50B guide (a miss caused by delayed third-party capacity). The FY2027 guidance (operating margin down less than 1 point, tax about 20%, FCF positive) and the CY2026 capex of about 170B are left out (review_trace). growth_anchor and current_fiscal_year therefore lack the actual/guided-midpoint ratio required by check 2. The anchor itself, 92,279M plus the Q2 midpoint of 96,550M plus two sequential quarters at +4.6% for 395.5B (+19.2%), is close to a seasonal extrapolation (about 394B) and is not changed by this.
findings.where: gather/numbers.json guidance_track (empty); casefile fc.anchors.current_fiscal_year; gather/documents.json guidance
findings.fix: Add the Q1 FY2027 guidance_track rows (revenue ratio about 1.02, capex below guide) and the FY2027 operating-margin, tax and FCF guidance and CY2026 capex rows listed by review_trace. Read the revenue guide as a modest floor.

findings.finding: Checked whether the finance-lease debt-like claim is double counted with balance-sheet debt. It is not. The 10-Q debt note gives Total debt of 35,481M (long-term debt 31,090M plus current portion 4,391M; casefile qa.fields.debt 35,481M, method noncurrent+current). The finance-lease liabilities of 70,973M (5,005M other current plus 65,968M other long-term) sit in other liabilities, outside the debt lines (10-Q lease note, 'Total finance lease liabilities $ 70,973'). The 21,719M of operating-lease liabilities is excluded from both, and the related costs stay in opex. The 70,973M is correctly sourced.
findings.where: inputs.json forecast.debt_like_claims[0]; casefile qa.fields.debt / qa.resolved.lease_liabilities; reading/10q_2026-10-28.txt debt note and lease note
findings.fix: None for the claim itself. Its consistency with reinvestment is the critical finding above.
